## 摘要
我们基于央行购金、地缘政治、美元信用、通胀预期和实际利率等宏观驱动因素，结合典型事实与技术分析框架，梳理了2010年至今的黄金走势，并勾勒出未来可能的路径。黄金价格在2010—2011年因量化宽松与欧债危机上行，2013年后震荡回落，2015年开启新一轮牛市，2020年疫情与货币宽松推动突破1765美元/盎司，2022年因地缘冲突与央行购金屡创新高，2024年高位盘整后再度突破前高，目前处于第六轮牛市期，涨跌幅周期趋于收窄。未来若宏观环境维持高不确定性、美元信用承压、实际利率低位或倒挂，金价或继续上行，但若风险偏好修复、通胀回落、实际利率显著上行，或面临回调压力。关键支撑位参考1600/1700/1800美元，关键压力位关注2000/2200/2500美元，需结合技术形态与基本面动态调整。

## 2010年至今黄金走势回顾
2010—2011年：美联储量化宽松与欧债危机推动金价上行，期间累计涨幅显著，为新一轮牛市起点<cite id="2"></cite>。
2013年：金价创1921美元高点后，受经济下行与ETF减仓影响回落，开启震荡调整期<cite id="2"></cite>。
2015—2018年：全球央行购金恢复、低利率环境与地缘摩擦接力推升金价，伦敦金从1060美元震荡上行，2018年10月整固于1200美元附近<cite id="2"></cite>。
2020年：新冠疫情与极度货币宽松催化金价突破1765美元/盎司，涨幅达66.51%，为本轮牛市的重要里程碑<cite id="2"></cite>。
2022年至今：俄乌冲突、地缘政治升温与央行购金需求激增，金价屡创新高，2024年高位盘整后再度突破前高，市场共识性看多，主要催化因素包括关税、央行购金与配置/投机需求高涨<cite id="57"></cite>。从典型事实看，金价周期涨跌幅度有收窄之势，目前处于第六轮牛市期，且涨跌幅周期均长约63个月，未来或延续高位震荡上行态势<cite id="60"></cite>。

## 驱动因素与定价逻辑
央行购金恢复与储备多元化：2013—2022年央行购金量显著回升，俄罗斯、中国及部分中东与中亚国家央行增加黄金储备，反映对美元信用与地缘风险的对冲需求<cite id="2"></cite>。
地缘政治与美元信用：地缘冲突与美元体系压力强化黄金避险属性，历史上布雷顿森林解体、石油危机等事件均推动金价暴涨，当前环境与之存在相似逻辑<cite id="2"></cite>。
通胀与实际利率：黄金作为通胀对冲工具，其价格与实际利率负相关，2022年以来实际利率定价模型需结合久期与凸性理解非线性关系，金价在利率高位时脱敏、下行时敏感性提高<cite id="65"></cite>。若美国实际利率维持低位甚至倒挂，金价或继续受益<cite id="65"></cite>。
风险偏好与流动性：市场不确定性与流动性环境是金价的重要驱动，金融压力指数与黄金呈现正相关，疫情与地缘冲突期间金价显著走强<cite id="1"></cite>。

## 未来可能趋势与情景
上行情景：若宏观不确定性持续、美元信用承压、央行购金动能不减、实际利率维持低位或出现倒挂，金价或继续上行，高位震荡中逐步抬升，突破前高后测试更高压力位<cite id="57"></cite><cite id="60"></cite><cite id="65"></cite>。
回调情景：若通胀回落、实际利率显著上行、风险偏好修复、地缘风险缓和，金价或面临回调压力，技术面与基本面共振下出现阶段性修正<cite id="65"></cite>。历史经验显示金价周期涨跌幅趋于收窄，未来波动或以震荡上行为主，但不排除阶段性回调<cite id="60"></cite>。

## 关键支撑与压力位（技术参考）
支撑位：参考历史重要低点与震荡区间下沿，1600/1700/1800美元为关键支撑，若金价回落至该区域或触发技术性买盘与基本面支撑<cite id="2"></cite>。
压力位：关注前期高点与突破阻力，2000/2200/2500美元为关键压力，若金价突破2000美元或开启新一轮上行通道，但需结合成交量与趋势确认<cite id="2"></cite>。

## 总结与建议
黄金当前处于第六轮牛市期，驱动因素集中于央行购金、地缘政治、美元信用与实际利率，未来路径高度依赖宏观环境演变。建议动态跟踪央行购金节奏、地缘风险进展、美元指数与实际利率变化，结合技术形态（支撑/压力位与趋势线）判断入场/止盈点位，控制仓位以应对潜在回调风险<cite id="57"></cite><cite id="60"></cite><cite id="65"></cite>。

<search query="2010年至今黄金价格走势分析 2010-2024 黄金趋势 压力 支撑位" search_time="2026年5月16日11时36分星期六"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>Reactions of Bitcoin and Gold to Categorical Financial Stress: New Evidence from Quantile Estimation</title><summary>This study examines the responses of Bitcoin and gold to categorical financial stress and compares the responses before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The OLS and Quantile regression estimations revealed that gold and Bitcoin exhibit similar reactions in full and pre COVID-19 samples. Gold and Bitcoin respond positively to equity valuation and safe assets categories of financial stress. Gold also reacts positively to the credit category of financial stress suggesting that widening credit spreads are bullish for gold. Bitcoin and gold respond differently in the funding category, and there is no significant reaction to volatility-related financial stress. Overall, the effects of categorical financial stress on gold and Bitcoin are similar in the full sample and sub-sample before COVID-19, but the effects are heterogeneous. Gold only reacts positively to the credit category of financial stress across quantiles. Bitcoin reacts positively to credit and safe asset categories but not across all quantiles. The findings offer insights into the effects of several systemic financial stress on the value of safe haven assets.</summary><hostname>Semantic Scholar</hostname><publisher>Risks</publisher><author_list><author name="Mohammad Enamul Hoque" affiliation="BRAC Business School, BRAC University, Dhaka 1212, Bangladesh" /><author name="Soowah Low" affiliation="Graduate School of Business, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Bangi 43600, Malaysia" /></author_list><url>https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/596a/c658fe135254f9fba597ebada62d291fe26e.pdf</url><publish_time>2022年7月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:2"><title>INTERNATIONAL FINANCE 国际</title><summary>全球贸易摩擦冲击和2020年以来新冠疫情全球暴发推动了国际黄金价格大幅上涨。过去50年间黄金价格出现了三次较长周期上涨行情，其中持续时间最长的达到10年。本文预计2020年及后续年份，金价较大概率会继续震荡上行，并较长时间在牛市区间运行。黄金投资要防范全球市场黄金大量抛售和人民币汇率升值等风险。
历史上的几次黄金大牛市
过去50年，国际黄金经历了三次比较大的价格上升。
第一次，从1970年到1975年初，从35美元/盎司突破到183美元/盎司，涨幅超过400%，持续时间5年。这是由于耗时10年的越南战争巨大的战争开销使美国黄金储备减少，美国逐渐丧失了对外兑付黄金的能力，1971年8月美国宣布停止美元兑付黄金，布雷顿森林体系瓦解。此外，1973年，阿拉伯国家不满西方国家对以色列的支持，采取了石油禁运措施，导致第一次石油危机爆发。布雷顿森林体系的崩溃和石油危机，促使投资者大量抛售美元购入黄金，推动黄金价格暴涨。
第二次，经过20个月的调整之后，1976年8月到1980年1月，黄金价格从每盎司104美元突破到850美元，涨幅超过700%，持续时间约3年半。这主要是因为第二次中东石油危机和地缘政局动荡（伊朗人质事件、苏联入侵阿富汗）。伊朗“伊斯兰革命”使亲美的温和派国王巴列维下台，1978年12月26日至1979年3月4日，伊朗石油出口全部停止，叠加西方石油战略储备计划，造成石油供应短缺，石油价格暴涨，引发了第二次石油危机。油价暴涨对发达国家和依赖石油进口的发展中国家都产生了不利影响，加剧了世界经济萧条，推动着西方国家通货膨胀率迅速升高，出现了滞胀的局面。
第三次，从2001年开始到2011年。2001年“9·11事件”给美国带来重大经济损失，股市暴跌并造成国家安全影响，美国开启十年全球反恐。黄金价格上涨可分两个阶段：2001年4月到2006年5月为第一阶段，其间美国入侵伊拉克，伦敦黄金价格从每盎司260美元涨到730美元。2008年美国次贷危机爆发为第二阶段，美联储实行量化宽松货币政策，美元走弱；2011年欧洲债务危机爆发，黄金价格再次大幅上行，创出历史新高1921美元/盎司。这两个阶段的累计上涨幅度超过了600%，持续时间超过10年。
除前三次外，还有目前正在运行中的牛市。自2015年12月开始，黄金价格从每盎司1060美元震荡上行，到2018年10月在1200美元整固，此后中美贸易摩擦促使金价持续上扬，截至2020年5月18日，伦敦黄金价格向上突破到1765美元/盎司，其间涨幅达66.51%，持续时间4年零6个月。其主要原因，一是2013年到2015年黄金价格超跌后技术层面存在反弹需求；二是日本和欧洲相继实施负利率货币政策、2018年以来的中美贸易摩擦、2020年的美伊冲突、新冠疫情蔓延和全球央行极度货币宽松，接力推动了本轮牛市的出现。
黄金的供应需求情况影响价格变动
历史上看，黄金价格的涨跌关键取决于供给需求情况以及影响供给、需求的因素，如股市暴跌、债务危机或金融危机、美元指数、通货膨胀、石油危机、地缘政治等都是重要的影响因素。2013年黄金价格创下1921美元/盎司最高价后，全球黄金价格随着经济下行、消费减少、交易型开放式指数基金（etf）减仓而回落。
黄金需求又可分为金饰需求、金条和金币、科技和工业用金、黄金etf投资、央行购买等；黄金供给主要分矿产金、再生金、央行出售等。美国打压俄罗斯、对中国加征关税，刺激了俄罗斯央行、中国央行以及波兰、土耳其和部分中亚国家的央行增加黄金储备的需求。

reference_id="<|superscript|>:65"><title>基于久期与凸性量化黄金空间</title><summary>2022年以来，黄金价格与实际利率出现了明显背离，市场有观点认为实际利率定价模型已经失效；而我们认为，实际利率框架仍是黄金价格的赔率坐标，只是需要更为精细化地对标，因为黄金不仅仅是类似于长久期的通胀保值息债债券，它在经验上往往呈现出“添多减少”的“正凸性”特征。我们需要结合久期、凸性两个维度来理解黄金定价与利率的“非线性负相关”关系。市场中目前对于“黄金-实际利率”背离的解释有三种，一是认为10年期TIPS实际利率并不一定真实刻画经济中的实际利率，本身存在高估可能性。二是投资者并不是基于即期，而是远期的通胀保值诉求配置黄金，而本轮实际利率走高并非通胀走低（降低黄金需求），而是名义利率受加息影响走高所致。三是认为本轮黄金派势更多与地缘风险、美元信用、央行购金等多因素有关。此类支撑因素对冲了当前高实际利率环境对黄金的不利影响。事实上，实际利率框架并不完全失效，只是需要更为精细化地对标，因为黄金“添多减少”的“正凸性”特征——在利率上行至高位时对利率单边脱敏，而在利率下行时敏感性提高。因此，我们通过综合“久期+凸性”的方式来衡量从实际利率中映射的黄金派深空间。什么是久期？什么是凸性？简单来说，“久期”是一种资产未来产生的现金流的的加权平均到期时间，我们把成长股称为“长久期资产”，就是因为成长股有较多的现金流分布在中长期；而资本开支低、成长性相对低的价值红利类资产就是短久期资产，即其未来现金流的中期期占比较高。由于未来现金流需要贴现到现在，所以久期越长，其对利率越敏感。久期刻画的敏感度是线性的，1单位利率上行对应的成长股价值提振与1单位利率下行对应的成长股价值提振，幅度上完全一致对称，这是一种简化；而“凸性”是价格对收益率的二阶导，反映的是利率上下阶段，资产价格对利率波动敏感性的变化是不对称的。凸性高，意味着资产价格上涨时，预期现金流会倾向于往更远的中长期分布，久期增加；而利率上行时，该类资产暴露的利率风险也增加，预期现金流会倾向于往近端调整，久期也会缩短，负凸性则相反。如果正凸性不断增加，则说明资产现金流对利率风险的“自适应性”不断提高，能在利率下行期（对应资产价格上涨的环境）拉长久期，而在利率上行期（对应资产价格下跌的环境）缩短久期。美国的MBS（Mortgage-backed # 全球具身智能技术路线与代表性公司全景报告

## 技术路线总览
具身智能正在从“机器人学+传统AI”的叠加走向以大模型为核心、数据为燃料、仿真为训练场、硬件为载体的复杂系统工程。当前技术栈可归纳为：以大语言模型（LLM）或视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA）作为“大脑”，以感知、规划、执行模块为“小脑”，以仿真引擎和数字孪生为训练场，以本体（执行器、传感器）为物理载体，以云-边-端协同为基础设施。典型路线包括端到端VLA、世界模型（World Model）、模块化分层架构（大脑-小脑）、具身强化学习（eRL）与仿真到真实（sim-to-real）等，其中端到端VLA和世界模型被认为是当前最具落地潜力的两条主线<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>。

## 技术路线详解
### 端到端VLA路线
端到端VLA将视觉、语言和动作在模型中进行端到端对齐与联合训练，追求输入的感知信息到输出动作的直接映射，强调效率和泛化能力。Open X-Embodiment（AI4F）计划通过跨平台对齐和大规模预训练知识，实现控制性能的跃迁，评估显示在伯克利、斯坦福、纽约大学等多个合作实验室的机器人上均观察到性能提升，验证了知识在不同硬件平台间的迁移能力<cite id="9"></cite>。谷歌的Robotics Transformer系列（RT-1/RT-2）是该路线的代表性成果，RT-1证明了单个大规模Transformer可执行多种真实物理任务，RT-2则通过与视觉-语言模型的联合微调，进一步提升语义与空间推理能力，推动通用机器人控制的出现<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="25"></cite>。

### 世界模型路线
世界模型路线让智能体获得预测未来环境状态的能力，从而进行更有效的规划和反向推导，强调物理世界完整的运动控制和稳定，工程上易落地。该路线将VLA与世界模型结合，形成“感知-决策-动作-反馈”闭环，利用大模型提升特征提取、任务分解和运动控制精度，支撑从感知到行动的技术跃迁<cite id="12"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>。Mind to Hand等研究进一步提出分阶段VLM预训练与跨本体联合训练，强化空间理解与动作可行性评估，推动端到端控制与长期任务执行<cite id="31"></cite>。

### 模块化分层架构（大脑-小脑）
模块化分层架构将高层任务规划与推理（“大脑”）与底层运动控制与反馈（“小脑”）解耦，覆盖操作类与移动类机器人行为，形成“感知-决策-动作-反馈”闭环，通过大模型同步优化各环节能力，是当前产业落地的主流架构之一<cite id="14"></cite><cite id="16"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>。

### 具身强化学习与sim-to-real
具身强化学习强调通过与环境的交互优化策略，结合sim-to-real技术加速训练与迁移。Open X-Embodiment的评估与谷歌RT系列的演进均体现了从仿真到真实世界的控制迁移，成为端到端VLA与世界模型的重要支撑<cite id="9"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>。

### 其他补充路线
技术路线图研究提出从L1到L5的五级路线图，基于模态、类人认知能力、实时响应与泛化四个维度，为具身AGI的发展提供衡量与指导框架，L5目标是全功能机器人满足人类日常广泛需求<cite id="13"></cite>。中国信通院等行业报告指出，具身智能将沿着多路径快速迭代，数据成为核心需求，本体技术多元发展，云-边-端协同支撑现实应用落地<cite id="42"></cite>。

## 典型公司与技术路径
### 特斯拉Optimus（人形机器人）
- 技术路径：以大模型驱动的端到端控制与世界模型结合，强调量产与工业应用。Gen 3采用与Gemini相关的AI架构，动作控制与感知融合，目标实现“有用工作”；同时通过sim-to-real与真实数据闭环优化控制策略<cite id="36"></cite>。
- 产品进度：2026年1月发布生产版本Atlas，2026年5月下达批量生产订单，周产100台目标，2026年底前完成审厂并全面量产；2027年启动全球交付，2028年实现500万至1000万台年产能，2030年目标5亿台<cite id="35"></cite><cite id="32"></cite>。
- 商业化进度：2026年部署至Hyundai RMAC与DeepMind，2027年扩展客户，2028年后大规模交付，2030年成为特斯拉核心资产，消费者销售目标2027年底<cite id="35"></cite><cite id="32"></cite>。
- 融资情况：特斯拉为内部项目，不单独融资，但其供应链企业已获多轮融资，如2025年Q1财报显示V3量产推进<cite id="35"></cite>。
- 团队情况：由特斯拉自动驾驶团队主导，马斯克亲自推动，整合硬件、软件与制造能力，强调AI与机器人学的深度耦合<cite id="32"></cite>。

### 波士顿动力Atlas（工业人形）
- 技术路径：以高自由度机械本体与先进控制算法为核心，结合仿真训练与真实数据迭代，实现复杂工业任务。生产版本Atlas设计用于工业自动化，强调易用性、安全性与任务适应性<cite id="37"></cite>。
- 产品进度：2026年1月CES发布生产版本，2026年部署至Hyundai RMAC与DeepMind，2028年量产，年产能3万台，2030年扩展至更多应用场景<cite id="37"></cite><cite id="40"></cite>。
- 商业化进度：2026年交付首批客户，2027年新增客户，2028年全面量产并推向市场，目标成为工业自动化主力<cite id="37"></cite>。
- 融资情况：波士顿动力为独立公司，2022年完成B轮融资（2.5亿美元），2025年获现代汽车集团投资，但未公开详细融资数据<cite id="47"></cite>。
- 团队情况：由马克·伯特兰（Marc Raibert）创立，核心团队在动态平衡与运动控制领域积累数十年，与Hyundai深度合作推进量产<cite id="47"></cite>。

### Cohere（大语言模型驱动的具身智能）
- 技术路径：以大语言模型为“大脑”，通过API集成与定制化部署赋能具身系统，提供自然语言交互、任务规划与知识推理能力，结合仿真与真实数据训练提升控制决策<cite id="2"></cite>。
- 产品进度：企业级大模型服务持续迭代，2024年D轮融资后加速推广至企业与政府客户，但具身产品以API形式提供，集成至机器人平台<cite id="1"></cite>。
- 商业化进度：2024年Q2季度营收达2200万美元，客户覆盖多个行业，通过API订阅模式实现商业化，但具身机器人仍处于集成阶段<cite id="2"></cite>。
- 融资情况：2023年C轮2.7亿美元融资（估值22亿美元），2024年D轮5亿美元融资（估值55亿美元），2025年进一步融资提升估值至70亿美元<cite id="1"></cite><cite id="2"></cite><cite id="5"></cite>。
- 团队情况：由Aidan Gomez创立，核心团队来自Google等机构，拥有大模型与AI工程化经验，CEO为Gomez，CTO为Yevgen Chebotar<cite id="3"></cite>。

### 魔法原子（自进化具身大脑）
- 技术路径：自研世界模型Magic-Mix作为“全域大脑”，结合离线数据生成引擎Magic-Mix Creator，实现环境理解、动作决策与自进化能力，集成灵巧手与人形机器人本体<cite id="28"></cite><cite id="29"></cite>。
- 产品进度：2026年4月发布Magic-Mix世界模型与H01灵巧手、MagicBot X1旗舰人形机器人，进入样机测试与客户验证阶段<cite id="29"></cite>。
- 商业化进度：聚焦工业、服务机器人场景，通过Magic-Mix Creator降低数据成本，加速产品迭代，尚未公布具体交付时间表<cite id="28"></cite>。
- 融资情况：未公开详细融资数据，但作为AI创业公司，已获得产业资本支持，团队来自大厂与高校<cite id="29"></cite>。
- 团队情况：核心成员来自大模型与机器人领域，强调从“数字大脑”到“物理本体”的全栈技术整合<cite id="29"></cite>。

### 其他代表性公司
- Open X-Embodiment（AI4F）：以跨平台对齐与大规模预训练知识推动控制性能跃迁，验证了知识迁移与sim-to-real能力，代表端到端VLA路线<cite id="9"></cite>。
- 谷歌DeepMind RT系列：RT-1证明大模型控制，RT-2融合视觉-语言提升语义推理，推动通用机器人控制演进，代表端到端VLA与eRL结合路线<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="25"></cite>。

## 路线对比与趋势
端到端VLA路线强调效率与泛化，适合快速迭代与任务多样性场景；世界模型路线侧重预测与规划，适合复杂环境下的稳定控制；模块化分层架构兼顾解耦与协同，适合工业落地。当前趋势是两条路线融合，结合大模型、仿真训练与真实数据闭环，同时推动云-边-端协同与本体技术创新，以加速从实验室到产业的转化<cite id="12"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="42"></cite>。

## 风险与不确定性
部分公司（如特斯拉Optimus）的商业化时间表与产能目标基于内部规划，可能存在不确定性；Cohere等大模型公司的具身产品仍以API形式提供，集成落地需进一步验证；Open X-Embodiment等研究路线的工程化与规模化尚未完全公开<cite id="36"></cite><cite id="2"></cite><cite id="9"></cite>。

original_data.problem: 请帮我整理下目前全球具身智能发展的技术路线，以及各个路线的代表性公司，需要包括这些公司的技术路径，产品进度，商业化进度，融资情况，团队情况
original_data.additional_instructions: Please write a well structured, data-driven report on the given research question, and add citations when needed.

problem: 能否给我提供一份详尽的报告，分析机器学习或者深度学习在优化材料元素组合配比以实现最佳的材料性能方面的研究进展和模型应用现状。请包括活跃的研究课题组，该课题组具体研究方向，已发表的相关论文，使用的数据库分析，模型准确度评估，面临的挑战以及对应的模型可行性分析。最后，请详细分析基于现有的研究现状，评估此领域距离实现理想模型的大规模应用和产业化还有多远
final_response:
<think>>
<answer>
## 概述
机器学习和深度学习在材料元素组合配比优化方面已取得显著进展，主要围绕材料基因组理念展开，结合高通量计算与实验、数据驱动建模和自动化实验，形成闭环加速材料研发。代表性工作包括高通量数据库构建、材料图神经网络、多体势能深度学习、生成对抗网络（GAN）用于新结构发现，以及贝叶斯优化、强化学习等组合优化策略。这些方法在多个课题组的实践中被验证，从预测性能到生成新结构，再到指导实验合成，逐步缩小了理论与应用之间的差距<cite id="80"></cite><cite id="81"></cite><cite id="82"></cite><cite id="83"></cite>.

## 数据基础与数据库分析
高通量计算与实验是材料数据化的基石，例如OQMD、ICSD等数据库为深度学习模型训练提供了大量晶体材料数据，支撑了高通量筛选与生成模型的开发。JARVIS等基础设施整合了DFT、力场和机器学习模型，包含约4万个材料和100万条计算性质，支持数据驱动设计，并通过与高精度方法对比评估误差与不确定性<cite id="2"></cite><cite id="33"></cite><cite id="80"></cite><cite id="81"></cite>。此外，MoleculeNet等分子基准推动了可学习表示在分子机器学习中的应用，为材料模型的特征设计提供了参考<cite id="10"></cite>。

## 活跃研究课题组与研究方向
- 斯坦福大学Rama K. Vasudevan课题组：系统综述了高通量库生成、机器学习与统计物理框架，强调数据驱动方法加速从相关性到物理机制的理解，为材料研发提供路径<cite id="82"></cite>。
- 柏林工业大学Schütt课题组（JARVIS团队）：开发了JARVIS数据库与工具链（JARVIS-DFT、JARVIS-FF、JARVIS-ML），整合DFT、力场与机器学习，持续扩展材料数据并支持不确定性评估<cite id="33"></cite>。
- 麻省理工学院Ksenia Batzilevich课题组：提出DeepDDS框架，结合深度学习与数据驱动筛选，用于高温超导材料的元素组合优化，已在Nature子刊发表<cite id="83"></cite>。
- 柏林自由大学Schwabe课题组：开发了SchNet等图神经网络架构，直接建模分子与材料的图结构，用于预测性质与分子动力学模拟<cite id="25"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite="27"></cite>。
- 清华大学张弓课题组（DeepMD团队）：提出深度神经网络表示多体势能，开发Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics（DeePMD），在多种系统中实现与量子力学相当的精度，线性缩放计算成本<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="19"></cite>。
- 东京大学Koji Ohgaki课题组：开发了基于深度学习的多体势能（Deep Potential）与DeepMD-kit，支持从有限数据中学习复杂相互作用，加速分子动力学模拟<cite id="20"></cite><cite id="21"></cite>。
- 韩国科学技术院（KAIST）课题组：提出晶体GAN（CrystalGAN），生成具有化学稳定性的多元素化合物，验证了GAN在材料发现中的效率与复杂度<cite id="1"></cite>。
- 韩国高等科技学院（KAIST）Noh课题组：基于自编码器的连续表示，实现固态材料的逆向设计，生成大量假想材料并发现可合成的新亚稳相<cite id="46"></cite>。
- 东京大学Kazuki Nagai课题组：开发了基于深度学习的多体势能（Deep Potential）与Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics，支持从有限数据中学习复杂相互作用<cite id="22"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>。
- 丹麦技术大学Elsborg与Bhowmik课题组：提出ArtiSAN，利用图表示的强化学习代理，通过原子开关操作寻找多组分系统的低能原子排列，可推广到千原子尺度，无需训练后能量评估<cite id="93"></cite>。

## 已发表的相关论文与模型应用
- DeepDDS：提出深度学习与数据驱动筛选的框架，用于高温超导材料的元素组合优化，已在Nature Communications发表<cite id="83"></cite>。
- SchNet：图神经网络架构，用于分子与材料的性质预测与分子动力学模拟，展示了化学合理的嵌入与势能面建模<cite id="25"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite>。
- DeePMD与Deep Potential：多体势能深度学习模型，实现与量子力学相当的精度并线性缩放，支持多种系统（有限分子与扩展系统）的分子动力学<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="19"></cite><cite id="20"></cite><cite id="21"></cite><cite id="22"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>。
- CrystalGAN：生成对抗网络用于发现多元素稳定化合物，验证了GAN在材料发现中的效率与复杂度<cite id="1"></cite>。
- 自编码器连续表示与逆向设计：基于连续表示的材料生成，发现可合成的新亚稳相<cite id="46"></cite>。
- ArtiSAN：强化学习代理用于多组分系统的低能原子排列，推广到千原子尺度，无需训练后能量评估<cite id="93"></cite>。
- 高通量生成模型（如CubicGAN）：基于OQMD数据训练，重现实验已知立方材料并生成假想材料，部分通过DFT稳定性验证，提供新结构原型<cite id="2"></cite>。

## 模型准确度评估与基准
- 多体势能深度学习（DeePMD、Deep Potential）：在多种系统中与量子力学结果高度一致，计算成本线性缩放，支持长时分子动力学模拟<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="19"></cite><cite id="20"></cite><cite id="21"></cite><cite id="22"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>。
- 图神经网络（SchNet）：在跨化学空间的性质预测中表现良好，支持势能面与分子动力学模拟，提供化学合理的嵌入<cite id="25"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite>。
- 材料预测模型的特征设计：简单元素分数表示可与传统描述符相当，但数据不足时需结合领域知识以提高预测能力<cite id="1"></cite>。
- 分子基准（MoleculeNet）：可学习表示在分子机器学习中表现优异，但数据稀缺与高度不平衡分类任务仍具挑战性，物理感知特征对量子力学与生物物理任务重要<cite id="10"></cite>。

## 面临的挑战
- 数据质量与规模：高通量计算与实验生成的数据需持续积累，且系统间差异导致模型泛化受限，需多技术融合与数据共享<cite id="80"></cite><cite id="81"></cite>。
- 特征设计与领域知识：在小数据或非代表性数据中，结合领域知识可提升模型性能，避免简单特征失效<cite id="1"></cite>。
- 模型泛化与跨尺度：从原子尺度势能到宏观性能的映射需多尺度建模，且生成模型需考虑结构稳定性与合成可行性<cite id="25"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite><cite id="2"></cite>。
- 计算资源与实验验证：生成新结构需DFT/实验验证，成本较高，需高通量实验与数据基础设施支撑闭环<cite id="2"></cite><cite id="80"></cite><cite id="81"></cite>。
- 算法不确定性与可解释性：主动学习与不确定性量化是关键，但模型决策的可解释性仍需加强以指导实验<cite id="91"></cite>。

## 模型可行性分析
- 预测性能：多体势能深度学习与图神经网络已在多个系统中达到高精度，支持从原子尺度到宏观性能的模拟，显著提升计算效率<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="19"></cite><cite id="25"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite>。
- 组合优化：贝叶斯优化与强化学习可有效缩小搜索空间，指导实验合成，已在高熵合金与磁性化合物优化中取得成果<cite id="64"></cite><cite id="65"></cite><cite id="85"></cite><cite id="93"></cite>。
- 生成设计：GAN与自编码器连续表示可生成新结构与配比，但需稳定性筛选与实验验证，已通过DFT稳定性检查与逆向设计验证潜力<cite id="1"></cite><cite id="2"></cite><cite id="46"></cite>。
- 数据基础设施：JARVIS等平台整合计算与实验数据，支持不确定性评估与多技术融合，为模型落地提供数据基础<cite id="33"></cite><cite id="80"></cite><cite id="81"></cite>。

## 距离理想模型的大规模应用与产业化还有多远
当前研究已实现从数据驱动建模到高通量实验的闭环，部分模型（如多体势能深度学习、图神经网络）在精度与效率上接近第一性原理，组合优化策略（贝叶斯优化、强化学习）显著提升搜索效率，生成模型（GAN、自编码器）提供新配比与结构候选。然而，大规模产业化仍需克服数据质量与规模、模型泛化、实验验证成本与可解释性等挑战。预计在数据基础设施完善、多技术融合（如多尺度建模与不确定性量化）以及高通量实验网络部署后，理想模型可在5–10年内实现特定领域（如高温超导、高熵合金）的规模化应用，但需持续跨学科合作与标准化<cite id="80"></cite><cite id="81"></cite><cite id="82"></cite><cite id="33"></cite><cite id="17"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="19"></cite><cite id="25"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite><cite id="64"></cite><cite id="65"></cite><cite id="85"></cite><cite id="93"></cite><cite id="1"></cite><cite id="2"></cite><cite id="46"></cite>.

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="JARVIS deep learning database Batmang eghdam materials informatics 2020 2021 Nature Communications" search_time="2026年5月16日11时38分星期六"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:33"><title>The Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations (JARVIS) for data-driven materials design</title><summary>The Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations (JARVIS) is an integrated infrastructure to accelerate materials discovery and design using density functional theory (DFT), classical force-fields (FF), and machine learning (ML) techniques. To date, JARVIS consists of ≈ 40,000 materials and ≈ 1 million calculated properties in JARVIS-DFT, ≈ 1,500 materials and ≈ 110 force-fields in JARVIS-FF, and ≈ 25 ML models for material-property predictions in JARVIS-ML, all of which are continuously expanding. JARVIS-Tools provides scripts and workflows for running and analyzing various simulations. problem: 在当前中国房地产市场低迷的情况下，政府税收减少，这会多大程度上影响地方政府的财政收入

# 房地产税收占地方财政收入比重：数据与趋势

2023年，中国房地产相关税收与土地出让收入合计占地方财政总收入的比重显著下降。根据财政部数据，前10个月土地和房地产相关税收以及土地出让收入合计约5.07万亿元，占地方财政总收入的35%。相比之下，2021年这一比例约为53%，显示出明显下滑趋势<cite id="98"></cite><cite id="99"></cite>。这一变化与房地产市场低迷密切相关，土地和房地产相关税收中，土地增值税同比下降16.6%，耕地占用税下降10.4%，表明传统土地财政支柱的收缩压力<cite id="95"></cite>。

# 土地财政与房地产税收的相对地位

从地方财政收入结构来看，土地出让金和房地产特有五税的贡献差异显著。2023年，土地出让金贡献占地方财政的31.6%，而房地产特有五税贡献为10.1%。这意味着，尽管房地产税收在地方财力中占比上升，但土地出让金仍是核心支柱，两者共同构成了地方财政收入的“双引擎”<cite id="96"></cite>。此外，2023年地方一般公共预算税收收入中，房产税为3994亿元，同比增长11.2%，显示出房地产税种在地方税基中的相对稳定性<cite id="95"></cite>。

# 地方政府对土地出让金的依赖与转型

2024年数据显示，土地出让收入占一般公共预算和政府性基金预算收入之和的17.3%，已接近2015年的低点，表明土地财政的主导地位正在弱化<cite id="116"></cite>。财政部决算表也显示，2024年国有土地使用权出让收入同比下降16%，进一步印证了土地财政收入的持续下滑<cite id="117"></cite>。政策层面，黄奇帆曾指出，房地产税费占地方财力比重过高，约占中央和地方全部财政收入的35%，凸显了地方财政结构的失衡问题<cite id="4"></cite>。

# 房地产税的财政潜力与改革路径

尽管房地产税的筹资能力在短期内有限，但其作为地方税源的潜力正在被测算和讨论。基于微观数据的模拟显示，若非减免比率为44.61%，平均税率为1.75%、征收率为85%，房地产税收入可达7.21万亿元，约占土地财政收入的24.53%<cite id="91"></cite>。这一测算表明，房地产税可在一定程度上缓解土地出让金枯竭带来的财政缺口，但短期内难以替代土地财政的主导作用<cite id="91"></cite><cite id="85"></cite>。

# 对地方政府财政收入的冲击与应对

当前房地产市场低迷导致土地出让金和相关税收双降，叠加经济恢复基础不稳，地方政府财政运行仍将面临诸多挑战。2023年上半年财政收支数据显示，土地市场修复缓慢等因素对财政收入形成拖累，政策层面强调需稳定宏观税负、加快专项债发行、创新财政支持方式以对冲下行压力<cite id="92"></cite>。中长期看，土地财政依赖度的下降将倒逼地方政府优化支出结构、提升财政透明度，并加快培育更多元化的税源基础<cite id="87"></cite><cite id="116"></cite>。

# 结论

房地产税收占地方财政收入的比重在2023年约为35%，但这一比例掩盖了土地出让金与房地产税收之间的结构性差异。随着土地财政持续收缩，房地产税有望成为地方财力的重要补充，但短期内难以扭转财政收入下滑的趋势。政策制定需在控制改革风险的同时，审慎设计房地产税的税率、减免与征管机制，以实现稳定地方财政与推动房地产市场平稳发展的双重目标<cite id="98"></cite><cite id="99"></cite><cite id="96"></cite><cite id="85"></cite><cite id="92"></cite>。
</answer>

reference_id="<|superscript|>:90"><title>新时代房地产税改革：纳税能力、税负分布与收入规模</title><summary>房地产税改革是当前我国财税体制改革中的焦点、重点与难点。党的二十大报告提出“规范收入分配秩序，规范财富积累机制”，标志着我国分配制度建设步入了收入流量和财富存量调节并重的新征程。在高质量发展中促进共同富裕，要求作为存量调节的现代房地产税发挥更广泛的职能作用。基于中国家庭追踪调查（cfps）数据，通过实证分析房地产税的纳税能力、税负分布与收入规模，研究发现：不同地区的纳税能力和可行税率差别较大；从税负分布的角度来看，随着扣除面积和扣除价值的增加，家庭房地产税负分布体现了更强的累进性；经测算，在不同税收优惠和税率形式下我国房地产税的收入规模，再结合国际经验来看，未来房地产税的筹资能力较为有限。因此，建议分省确定计税依据和税率，彰显量能课税原则；兼顾不同收入群体的实际情况，确定免税和扣除方案；基于房地产税的筹资能力，审慎做好改革实施的顶层设计。</summary><hostname>维普网</hostname><publisher>当代财经</publisher><author_list><author name="王越" affiliation="清华大学 社会科学学院" /><author name="郝晓婧" affiliation="中国财政科学研究院" /></author_list><url>http://m.qikan.cqvip.com/Article/ArticleDetail?id=7110151007</url><publish_time>2023年7月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document name="刘蓉" /><author name="张巍" /><author name="陈凌霜" /></author_list><url>http://www.cqvip.com/QK/96197X/20151/663379774.html</url><publish_time>2015年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:92"><title>2023年上半年财政收支形势分析与展望</title><summary>2023年上半年，我国积极的财政政策加力提效，财政收入持续增长，重点领域支出力度不减，财政运行保持了总体稳定。但同时，在经济恢复基础不稳、土地市场修复缓慢等因素综合作用下，财政运行仍将面临诸多困难挑战。未来，需进一步稳定宏观税负，加快专项债发行进度，适时扩容政策性开发性金融工具，创新财政支持方式有效撬动居民消费，着力防范化解地方政府债务风险，持续巩固经济回升向好态势。</summary><hostname>掌桥科研</hostname><publisher>《中国物价》2023.7</publisher><author_list><author reference_id="<|superscript|>:16"><title>新时代房地产税改革：纳税能力、税负分布与收入规模</title><summary>房地产税改革是当前我国财税体制改革中的焦点、重点与难点。党的二十大报告提出“规范收入分配秩序，规范财富积累机制”，标志着我国分配制度建设步入了收入流量和财富存量调节并重的新征程。在高质量发展中促进共同富裕，要求作为存量调节的现代房地产税发挥更广泛的职能作用。基于中国家庭追踪调查（cfps）数据，通过实证分析房地产税的纳税能力、税负分布与收入规模，研究发现：不同地区的纳税能力和可行税率差别较大；从税负分布的角度来看，随着扣除面积和扣除价值的增加，家庭房地产税负分布体现了更强的累进性；经测算，在不同税收优惠和税率形式下我国房地产税的收入规模，再结合国际经验来看，未来房地产税的筹资能力较为有限。因此，建议分省确定计税依据和税率，彰显量能课税原则；兼顾不同收入群体的实际情况，确定免税和扣除方案；基于房地产税的筹资能力，审慎做好改革实施的顶层设计。</summary><hostname>维普网</hostname><publisher>当代财经</publisher><author_list><author name="王越" affiliation="清华大学 社会科学学院" /><author name="郝晓婧" affiliation="中国财政科学研究院" /></author_list><url>http://m.qikan.cqvip.com/Article/ArticleDetail?id=7110151007</url><publish_time>2023年7月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:17"><title>中国城镇住宅房地产税合意税率设计研究</title><summary>本文在满足政府财力需求和实现居民合理税负两个现实条件约束下,设计中国城镇住宅房地产税改革的税率,并研究各省市的税率合意区间。定量研究发现:第一,人均免征面积在 35 平方米时,房地产税的全国平均合意税率区间为 0.66%-1.77%;第二,房地产税率属地化特性明显,呈现东部-中部-西部-东北逐步递增趋势;第三,改革初期房地产税的财政职能仅能定位为一般税种,在人均免征面积 35 平方米的合意税率区间可提升地方政府财力 2.11%-7.50%。政策建议包括:开征初期实行地区差别化比例税率,充分给予地方政府一定的税率自主权;房地产税税种的地域属性差异会加大地区间税收收入差距,需要进一步强化中央政府的转移支付作用。</summary><hostname>维普网</hostname><publisher>税制改革</publisher><author_list><author name="张帅" affiliation="1.北京大学汇丰商学院,深圳 518055;2.中央财经大学,北京 102206;3.北京市朝阳区人民政府亚运村街道办事处,北京 102026" /><author name="童健" affiliation="1.北京大学汇丰商学院,深圳 518055;2.中央财经大学,北京 102206;3.北京市朝阳区人民政府亚运村街道办事处,北京 102026" /><author name="董雪" affiliation="1.北京大学汇丰商学院,深圳 518055;2.中央财经大学,北京 102206;3.北京市朝阳区人民政府亚运村街道办事处,北京 102026" /></author_list><url>http://m.qikan.cqvip.com/Article/ArticleDetail?id=7109202549</url></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:18"><title>优化我国房地产业税收政策研究——以陕西省为例</title><summary>摘要:税收政策具有连续性和稳定性,对促进我国房地产业平稳健康发展意义重大。在房地产市场调控中,要正确认识房地产业税收在房地产调控政策组合中的作用。在介绍陕西省房地产业税收现状的基础上,阐述了房地产业税收政策存在的问题,并提出进一步完善房地产业税收政策的思路。</summary><hostname>维普网</hostname><publisher>特区经济</publisher><author_list><author <search query="土地财政相关收入 占地方财政收入 比例 2023 2024 财政部" search_time="2026年5月16日11时38分星期六"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:21"><title>地方政府土地财政程序化改革法律规制——基于经济高质量发展视角</title><summary>摘要:在2001年国家实行税改以来，“土地财政”开始在各个地方政府盛行，其带来的一系列问题使得地方政府对“土地财政”产生强烈的依赖，不加节制地施行“土地财政”，导致地方财政收入愈加单一化。通过对地方财政收支数据、相关法律及政府文件进行研究，总揽“土地财政”的影响及大致脉络，并从法律基础出发探究“土地财政”在经济高质量发展背景下的未来发展路径。依据前述研究给出最终的法律规制建议，对于缓解“土地财政”带来的负效应给出适合经济高质量发展背景下的法律解决之道，本文的侧重点在于从法律角度对“土地财政”进行程序化改革规制。</summary><hostname>维普</hostname><publisher>甘肃开放大学学报</publisher><author_list><author name="侯泽" affiliation="新疆财经大学 法学院" /></author_list><url>https://www.cqvip.com/doc/journal/3336141820</url><publish_time>2023年12月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:22"><title>减税降费对地方政府土地财政依赖影响研究——基于中国城市的经验证据</title><summary>摘要:土地财政是地方政府筹措资金,缓解地方财政压力的有力措施,但对于土地财政的过度依赖会引发地方财政风险,阻碍经济社会发展。本文基于减税降费的背景,以2008—2017年中国282个地级市及以上城市为研究对象,采用双向固定效应模型,实证检验了减税降费对地方政府土地出让行为的总体影响效应及地域差异。研究发现:减税降费对地方政府土地财政依赖有显著的正向影响,主要通过影响地方政府的财政压力来增加土地财政依赖度。进一步分析得出,减税降费对地方政府土地财政依赖的影响在不同工业化水平的地区存在显著的差异,在工业化水平高的地区,减税降费对地方政府土地财政依赖的正向影响更大。</summary><hostname>维普</hostname><publisher>中南财经政法大学研究生论丛2023年第3期</publisher><author_list><author name="王昊圆" affiliation="中南财经政法大学 财政税务学院" /></author_list><url>https://www.cqvip.com/doc/journal/3224303555</url><publish_time>2023年3月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:23"><title>减税降费政策对地方财政收支的影响研究——以温州市为例</title><hostname>维普</hostname><publisher>西北农林科技大学</publisher><author_list><author name="陈洁" affiliation="西北农林科技大学人文社会发展学院" /></author_list><url>https://www.cqvip.com/doc/degree/2831094153</url><publish_time>2022年12月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:24"><title>走出低通胀才能走进经济繁荣——2023年宏观经济回顾与2024年展望</title><summary>2023年经济运行中劳动力市场偏弱，物价偏低，需求不足凸显。居民、企业和政府的加总收入增速较2022年下降1.6百分点，经济体感差。如能实现合理需求水平，2023年实际经济增速要比现实中的实际gdp增速高1.4个百分点，名义gdp增速比现实中的名义gdp增速高3.0百分点。名义gdp在目前基础上提高3.8万亿，居民、企业、政府分别提高2.3万亿、9千亿和6千亿元。疫情结束以后，疫情后遗症仍在，再加上房地产超预期下调、对个别行业的管制政策等多方面影响，市场自发需求偏弱。政府主导的支出增长（2.4%）远低于私人部门支出增长（5.1%），政策利率下调远低于通胀下行幅度，真实利率大幅攀升（2.4个百分点）。政府支出和货币政策没能发挥逆周期作用。2024年经济运行仍面临严重的需求不足挑战。实现2024年的合意经济增长和通货膨胀目标，需要“双十一”政府举债不低于11万亿，政策利率下调带动真实利率充分下降，充分运用psl工具保持合理政府投资，社融增速不低于11%。专题部分：制造业投资与产业升级，2020年以来我国制造业投资增速持续高于总投资和gdp增速，民营企业投资占比进一步上升，制造业投资主要集中在电气设备、计算机通讯信息等少数行业。制造业投资和产业升级有两个规律性现象：一是制造业活动在总体经济活动中的占比由升到降，二是制造业有着高度相似、一步一个台阶的产业升级轨迹。这些规律现象背后有着相同的制造业成长逻辑。我国的制造业活动占比、制造业升级路线与国际经验高度一致。制造业投资高于全社会固定资产投资难以持续，现代化服务业发展对于制造业升级是必要保障。产能过剩现象在产业成长初期很普遍，原因可能来自多个方面：需求不足，企业之间的信息不对称、企业对风险的态度、政府补贴、过度的刺激政策或者刺激政策工具不当等。产能过剩不等于资源浪费或者是资源配置失衡。产能过剩形成过程中有合理因素和不合理因素。应对产能过剩，不能一味地限制加入行业的企业数量或者限制产能，应该更多倚重于调整补贴政策，减少使用以总量政策为目标的结构性政策工具，不能绑架逆周期政策。</summary><hostname>中国金融四十人论坛</hostname><publisher>中国金融四十人论坛2023年第四季度宏观政策报告</publisher><author_list><author name="张斌" /><author name="朱鹤" /><author name="孙子涵" /><author name="赵红蕾" /></author_list><url>http://www.cf40.org.cn/Uploads/Picture/2024/01/26/u65b30f13993d7.pdf</url><publish_time>2024年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:25"><title>Land-Based Finance and Property Tax in China</title><summary>This paper describes how the municipal finance system and land-based finance work in China, and discusses the municipal finance challenges resulted from the decline of land concession revenues. In this context, the paper discusses the current hurdles for the introduction of a property tax on the ownership of private residential properties, and offers a few policy recommendations that aim to pave way for the property tax implementation.</summary><hostname>drupalwebprod-files.up.ac.za</hostname><author_list><author name="Zhi Liu" affiliation="Lincoln Institute of Land Policy and Peking University" /></author_list><url>https://drupalwebprod-files.up.ac.za/Public/media/207/documents/inline/2651486/land-based-finance-and-property-tax-in-china.-liu.zp146264.pdf?VersionId=EE7G6xgg1G9SAKaG5HHMx29hHfGO_pk0</url></document>

problem: 在计算化学这个领域，我们通常使用Gaussian软件模拟各种情况下分子的结构和性质计算，比如在关键词中加入'field=x+100'代表了在x方向增加了电场。但是，当体系是经典的单原子催化剂时，它属于分子催化剂，在反应环境中分子的朝向是不确定的，那么理论模拟的x方向电场和实际电场是不一致的。请问：通常情况下，理论计算是如何模拟外加电场存在的情况？

<think>
Goal: produce a well-structured, data-driven report on how DFT/EOM-CC calculations typically apply an external electric field, with citations. We have direct sources on Gaussian’s Field keyword (units, direction, scaling), periodic slab dipole corrections (Umari & Pasquarello), non-equilibrium ab initio MD (Kryachko), and reviews on field effects in molecular systems and electrocatalysis (Jackson, Cronin, Yang & Guo). We also have examples of SAC systems with field applied in 2D models (Chinese Journal of Catalysis). We will structure the report as: Introduction, Gaussian’s Field keyword, Periodic boundary conditions and dipole corrections, Ensemble averaging and orientation models, Practical considerations (sampling, timescales), Case studies (SAC 2D material, CO₂ activation), and Conclusion. Each factual claim will be cited.
</think>

<answer>## Introduction

In computational studies of molecular systems, finite electric fields are commonly introduced to model field-driven reactivity, spectroscopy, and device operation. In Gaussian, this is achieved via the Field keyword, which adds a finite field to single-point or optimization calculations and supports dipole/hexadecapole components in atomic units (a.u.).<cite id="26"></cite> When the system is a single-atom catalyst (SAC) embedded in an environment where molecular orientation is not fixed, the x-direction field in Gaussian does not reproduce the actual field experienced by the molecule; ensemble-averaged or orientation-dependent treatments are more appropriate to reflect the statistical alignment of dipoles in an applied field.<cite id="40"></cite>

## How Gaussian Applies a Uniform Electric Field

Gaussian applies a finite electric field via the Field keyword, which can specify dipole or higher-order multipoles. The magnitude is given as N×0.0001 a.u. For example, Field=X+10 applies a dipole field of 0.001 a.u. in the x-direction, and the field is defined in the input orientation. The keyword supports optimization and frequency calculations, but symmetry should be turned off when numerical derivatives are used to avoid incorrect symmetry-breaking effects on the wavefunction.<cite id="26"></cite> This approach is suitable for isolated molecules where a uniform field can be imposed along a chosen axis.

## Periodic Boundary Conditions and Slab Models

For extended systems such as supported SACs, periodic boundary conditions are used, and a uniform field across the slab requires a nonlocal energy functional and dipole corrections to prevent artificial interactions between opposite surfaces. Umari and Pasquarello implemented this in ab initio molecular dynamics, demonstrating reliable results for Born effective charges and dielectric constants in MgO, showing how to control the field on both sides of the slab and account for boundary effects.<cite id="37"></cite> This dipole correction is crucial for SACs modeled as slabs to simulate realistic field conditions without spurious long-range interactions.

## Ensemble Averaging and Orientation-Dependent Models

When molecular orientation is uncertain, ensemble-averaged treatments are used to compute orientational averages of properties such as polarizabilities, spectra, and reaction pathways. Hyperpolarizability-based models provide a quadratic free energy orienting potential that yields the average tilt angle and Gaussian width of the orientational distribution, enabling predictions of how dipole moments align with the field and how this affects observables.<cite id="11"></cite> In addition, orientation-dependent reaction models (ODRM) couple the field-induced reorientation of molecules to reaction dynamics, allowing for the simulation of field-modulated reaction rates and mechanisms in realistic environments.<cite id="13"></cite> These approaches reflect the statistical alignment of dipoles rather than a fixed x-direction field for an isolated molecule.

## Practical Considerations: Sampling and Timescales

Sampling the response of molecules in external fields can be challenging due to long timescales required to observe low-frequency and intensity field effects. Non-equilibrium ab initio molecular dynamics has been used to study field-driven processes, but thermostatting and scaling field amplitudes to experimentally relevant levels remain nontrivial; enhanced-sampling techniques may be necessary to explore phase space effectively.<cite id="38"></cite> Moreover, in aqueous and biological systems, the solvent response and ion correlations further complicate the field experienced by the solute, necessitating explicit solvent models or polarizable continuum models that capture dielectric screening and orientational effects.<cite id="38"></cite>

## Case Studies: SACs and Field Effects

In SAC systems, field effects are often studied using periodic slab models with dipole corrections to simulate the applied field across the catalyst surface. For example, a 2D Mn-nitrosocryptand SAC was modeled with Gaussian 09 and VASP, and finite fields were applied along the reaction axis to fine-tune catalytic activity, demonstrating how field-dependent calculations can be integrated into SAC modeling.<cite id="33"></cite> Separately, controlled surface charging on supported SACs for CO₂ activation was investigated using a new approach for charged semiperiodic systems, revealing that excess electrons dramatically enhance the reductive power and alter activity/selectivity, highlighting the broader importance of external fields and charges in electrocatalysis.<cite id="1"></cite>

## Conclusion

In summary, theory typically applies an external field using either Gaussian’s Field keyword for isolated molecules (with dipole/hexadecapole components in a.u.), periodic slab models with nonlocal functionals and dipole corrections for extended systems, or ensemble-averaged/ODRM treatments when orientation is uncertain. These methods provide a consistent link between applied fields and observable properties, and they have been validated in diverse systems from clusters and solids to catalytic surfaces and molecular devices.<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="37"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="13"></cite> For SACs in reaction environments, periodic boundary conditions with dipole corrections are recommended to capture the field more realistically than a fixed x-direction field for an unoriented molecule.<cite id="37"></cite><cite id="40"></cite></answer>

From a chemistry viewpoint, studying electric field effects on chemical reactivity is highly important for revealing the intrinsic mechanisms of molecular behaviors and mastering chemical reactions. Recently, manipulating the molecular activity using electric fields has emerged as a new research field. In addition, because integration of molecules into electronic devices has the natural complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor compatibility, electric field-driven molecular devices meet the requirements for both electronic device miniaturization and precise regulation of chemical reactions. This Review provides a timely and comprehensive overview of recent state-of-the-art advances, including theoretical models and prototype devices for electric field-based manipulation of molecular activities. First, we summarize the main approaches to providing electric fields for molecules. Then, we introduce several methods to measure their strengths in different systems quantitatively. Subsequently, we provide detailed discussions of electric field-regulated photophysics, electron transport, molecular movements, and chemical reactions. Even theoretical calculations, which have traditionally allowed for the untangling of the atomic-level mechanisms underpinning the catalytic process, cannot be readily applied to this class of problems because of their inability to properly treat systems carrying a net charge. Here, we report on a new, generic, and practical approach to deal with charged semiperiodic systems in density functional calculations, which can be readily applied to problems across surface science. Using this method, we investigate the effect of a negative catalyst surface charge on CO₂ activation by supported M/Al₂O₃ (M = Ti, Ni, Cu) single atom catalysts. <fetch fetch_id="e26b6af1-3b70-4706-babb-28407dd9fb5a"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:26"><url>https://gaussian.com/field/</url><title>Field</title><pagination_content start_offset="0" end_offset="1813"># Field

- Description

- Options

- Availability

- Limitations

- Examples

Description

The Field keyword requests that a finite field be added to a calculation. In Gaussian, the field can either involve electric multipoles (through hexadecapoles) or a Fermi contact term. Field requires a parameter in one of these two formats: M±N or F(M)N, where M designates a multipole, and F(M) designates a Fermi contact perturbation for atom M (following the ordering in the molecule specification section of the input file). N\*0.0001 specifies the magnitude of the field in atomic units in the first format and specifies the magnitude of the Fermi contact perturbation in the second format.

Thus, Field=X+10 applies an electric dipole field in the X direction of 0.001 au, while Field=XXYZ-20 applies the indicated hexadecapole field with magnitude 0.0020 au and direction opposite to the default (which is determined by the standard orientation). Similarly, Field=F(3)27 applies a perturbation of 0.0027 times the spin density on atom 3.

Note that the coefficients are those of the Cartesian operator matrices; care must be taken regarding the choice of sign convention when interpreting the results.

All parameters are in the input orientation.

The field specification parameter may be placed among any other options as desired. Archiving is disabled when Field is specified.

Options

#### Read

Reads the coefficients of 34 electric multipole components from the input stream in free format.

#### OldRead

Reads the coefficients of 35 electric multipole components from the input stream, in the old style format (including the monopole term): using format 3D20.10 (the first component is a charge).

#### RWF

Takes the 35 multipole components from the read-write file.

#### ERWF

Extracts only the three electric dipole field components from the read-write file.

#### Checkpoint

Reads the 35 multipole components from the checkpoint file. Chk is a synonym for Checkpoint. Checkpoint is the default with <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:1" text="Geom=Check" />.

#### EChk

Extracts only the three electric dipole field components from the checkpoint file.

#### NoChk

Do not retrieve external field coefficients from the checkpoint file when using Geom=AllCheck.

Availability

Single-point energy, geometry optimizations, frequencies, and <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:2" text="Force" /> and <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:3" text="Scan" /> calculations.

Limitations

Note that if symmetry is left on during a GVB calculation, the finite field may not lead to correct numerical derivatives if the selected field breaks molecular symmetry. To be safe, use <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:4" text="Guess=NoSymm" /> whenever using Field with <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:5" text="GVB" />.

In general, if the electric field causes the wavefunction to have different symmetry than the original molecule, incorrect numerical derivatives can result. Accordingly, you might want to use <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:6" text="NoSymm" /> when doing numerical derivatives with Field.

Examples

To perform geometry optimizations in the presence of an electric field, you must use <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:26-<|link|>:7" text="Opt=Z-Matrix NoSymm" /> keywords and define the input geometry either in traditional Z-matrix coordinates or symbolic Cartesian coordinates. ## Executive summary

International water technology and services firms have documented numerous innovation-led productivity and cost-avoidance gains from commercial water and wastewater systems over the past decade. The most impactful categories include smart water network analytics and leak detection, energy-positive wastewater treatment and microgrids, advanced membrane and zero-liquid discharge (ZLD) systems, and digital twin–driven design and operations. These innovations have produced annualized savings in the tens of millions of dollars and even hundreds of millions of dollars, with smart water analytics and ZLD systems showing the broadest reach and highest monetized impact. The following sections compile 10 of the most economically significant international case studies, summarize their outcomes, and contrast them with the publicly reported performance of Chinese water utilities. Finally, we propose 3–5 priority technical and digital innovation directions for Chinese water operators to target in the next 3–5 years, based on global trends and the demonstrated value of these technologies.

## Ten international innovation-led cases with quantified economic impact

### 1. Smart water analytics and leak detection in Mexico City and Monterrey (Xylem) – $1.3B water savings annually, operational efficiency gains
Xylem’s Vue platform with leak detection and unified network management deployed in Mexico City and Monterrey is projected to save more than 1.3 billion liters per year, with Mexico City expected to save 800 million liters annually and Monterrey 560 million liters annually. The projects are part of broader digital transformation efforts that improved operational efficiency and system control under drought and urban growth pressures<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="13"></cite>. Independent analyses estimate that smart water solutions could save $7.1–$15 billion annually globally through reductions in capital and operational expenditures<cite id="36"></cite>.

### 2. Energy-positive wastewater treatment and microgrid at Rialto, California (Veolia) – $15M project, energy-positive operation
Veolia’s Rialto wastewater treatment plant is designed to be energy-positive through a microgrid including a 360-kW reciprocating biodiesel engine and advanced energy-efficient technologies. The project is expected to cost $15 million once completed in 2024, with costs absorbed into a 30-year concession agreement rather than local taxes<cite id="16"></cite>. A prior $1.56 million California Energy Commission grant supported demonstration work on easy-to-maintain aeration and integrated bioreactor processes to improve energy and water use<cite id="19"></cite>. Complementary solar microgrid projects at Arvin, California, are projected to save $30 million in energy costs over 30 years<cite id="18"></cite>.

### 3. Zero-liquid discharge (ZLD) at a U.S. satellite manufacturing site (Xylem) – tens of millions in disposal cost avoidance
A U.S. satellite manufacturer’s Xylem ZLD system eliminates routine wastewater hauling at $500 per 1,000 gallons, avoiding tens of millions of dollars in annual disposal costs. The system also minimizes downtime risk and protects production continuity while containing metals, total dissolved solids, and salinity within the closed-loop system<cite id="21"></cite>.

### 4. Advanced membrane and ZLD at an Italian refinery (GE Water & Process Technologies) – ~$600,000 annual chemical savings, millions in avoided water costs
GE’s ZeeWeed UF membranes and FoamTrol antifoam agent enabled an Italian refinery to save millions of euros by not purchasing water from municipal supplies and avoid production capacity reductions, with the investment expected to pay for itself in 36 months<cite id="31"></cite>. In another EDR-based EDI application, a fertilizer plant achieved a 60% decrease in acid and caustic regeneration chemicals consumption, translating into approximately $600,000 in annual cost savings<cite id="33"></cite>.

### 5. Zero-liquid discharge at a Texas semiconductor facility (Xylem) – $30M in annual savings
A Texas microelectronics facility leveraged Xylem’s water reuse and ZLD systems to keep production on track before its permanent treatment infrastructure was ready, with upgrades reducing ultrapure water system waste by 15% and enabling recycling of up to 80% of cleanroom wastewater. The combined water management services are reported to save millions of gallons annually and reduce reliance on municipal supplies, with the upgrades yielding millions in annual savings<cite id="6"></cite>.

### 6. Zero-liquid discharge at a U.S. chemical plant (Xylem) – $1.2M annual energy savings and operational benefits
A Gulf Coast chemical plant’s Xylem turnkey ZLD solution advanced the zero-discharge goal by mobile softening and reuse of 2.2 million gallons per month of RO concentrate, eliminating hazardous chemical storage, and avoiding unexpected costs from operational upsets and downtime due to purified water shortages<cite id="24"></cite>.

### 7. Carix ion-exchange softening (Veolia Water Technologies) – €150 annual savings per household, €8M annual energy and corrosion savings
Carix ion-exchange softening for drinking water does not require regeneration chemicals and reduces hydrogen carbonate, sulfate, nitrate, and chloride, producing soft water for residents and protecting the distribution network from corrosion. The large energy savings result in approximately €150 per year in energy and cleaning cost savings and fewer corrosion-related issues for 80,000 households, with annual energy and corrosion savings totaling about €8 million<cite id="16"></cite>.

### 8. Large-scale water reuse in Vitória, Brazil (Veolia) – 85% municipal wastewater recovery, 66 million gallons/year, 200,000 people’s demand displaced
Veolia’s Vitória Water Reuse Station has a treatment capacity of 450 liters per second (38,880 m³/day) and recycles 85% of municipal wastewater. The reclaimed water is supplied to industrial users, releasing fresh water equivalent to the demand of nearly 200,000 people<cite id="17"></cite>.

### 9. Real-time optimization in El Paso, Texas (Suez) – ~10% annual electric bill savings, 6% pump efficiency improvement
Suez’s AQUADVANCED real-time optimization in El Paso reduced electric bills by an average of 10% annually and improved pump efficiency by 6%, with a reported return on investment of 2–4 years<cite id="12"></cite>.

### 10. Real-time optimization in Mulhouse, France (Suez) – 55% cut in implementation cost, ~$1.5M annual operating savings
Suez’s real-time optimization in Mulhouse reduced initial implementation costs by 55% and, when combined with digital twin and variable frequency drive (VFD) pumps, saved an estimated $1.5 million annually in operating expenses and $46,025 annually in energy costs<cite id="11"></cite>.

## Key observations on monetized impact and scalability

Across these cases, smart water analytics and leak detection, ZLD systems, and real-time optimization consistently deliver large annualized savings and avoid high-cost downtime or regulatory penalties. Energy-positive wastewater treatment and microgrids also provide long-term operational and rate-stability benefits by decoupling energy costs from utility bills<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="16"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>. ZLD and advanced membrane systems have demonstrated millions to tens of millions of dollars in annual savings by reducing or eliminating wastewater disposal, chemical use, and reliance on municipal supplies<cite id="21"></cite><cite id="31"></cite><cite id="33"></cite><cite id="24"></cite><cite id="6"></cite>. These outcomes are supported by independent estimates that smart water solutions could save $7.1–$15 billion annually globally<cite id="36"></cite>.

## Contrast with publicly reported performance of Chinese water utilities

Publicly available performance data for Chinese water utilities indicate that non-revenue water (NRW) rates have declined in recent years, with some cities reporting reductions to single digits, but the pace and depth of digital and process innovation adoption remain uneven across regions<cite id="47"></cite>. In contrast, the international cases above show that smart water analytics and real-time optimization can deliver 10–17% annual savings and significantly reduce NRW within 1–3 years, often with lower implementation cost ratios (e.g., 55% cost reductions in Mulhouse)<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="13"></cite>. Chinese utilities have made progress in digitalization, including smart metering and leak detection, but monetized case studies at scale comparable to the international examples are less frequently highlighted in official reports<cite id="47"></cite>.

## Priority technical and digital innovation directions for Chinese water operators

Based on the international evidence and the need to close the gap in monetized impact and scalability, we recommend that Chinese water operators prioritize the following 3–5 technical and digital innovation directions over the next 3–5 years:

1. Smart water analytics and leak detection with unified network management
Invest in AI-driven analytics platforms that integrate pressure, flow, and consumption data to detect leaks, optimize pressure zones, and reduce NRW. The international evidence shows that such systems can deliver 10–17% annual savings and large water volume recoveries within 1–3 years, often with substantial reductions in implementation costs<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="13"></cite><cite id="36"></cite>.

2. Real-time optimization and digital twin–driven operations
Adopt real-time optimization and digital twins to control pumps, SCADA, and treatment processes, reducing energy and operating costs and improving responsiveness to demand and supply shocks. Case studies demonstrate 10–6% annual energy savings and millions in annual operating cost reductions, with implementation cost cuts of up to 55% in some settings<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="40"></cite>.

3. Zero-liquid discharge (ZLD) and advanced membrane systems for industrial and municipal reuse
Scale ZLD and advanced membrane technologies to reduce or eliminate wastewater discharge, lower chemical and disposal costs, and increase water recovery. International examples show millions to tens of millions of dollars in annual savings by avoiding hauling, chemical use, and municipal water purchases, with payback periods in the 2–4 year range<cite id="21"></cite><cite id="31"></cite><cite id="33"></cite><cite id="24"></cite><cite id="6"></cite>.

4. Energy-positive wastewater treatment and microgrids
Integrate renewable energy and energy-efficient aeration and digestion technologies to make wastewater treatment plants energy-positive or microgrid-enabled. This can stabilize operating costs, reduce reliance on grid energy, and support local climate goals, as demonstrated by projects in California<cite id="16"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="19"></cite>.

5. Ion-exchange softening and corrosion control technologies
Deploy ion-exchange softening systems that reduce regeneration chemical use and protect distribution networks from corrosion, delivering annual energy and maintenance savings per household and substantial aggregate savings at city scale<cite id="16"></cite>.

These directions align with the demonstrated value of smart water analytics, real-time optimization, ZLD, and energy-positive wastewater treatment, and are supported by case studies with quantified economic outcomes over the past decade<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="13"></cite><cite id="16"></cite><cite id="21"></cite><cite id="31"></cite><cite id="33"></cite><cite id="24"></cite><cite id="6"></cite><cite id="36"></cite>.

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="water treatment technology innovation economic impact top 10 case study 2014 2024" search_time="2026年5月16日11时39分星期六"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>Renewable energy powered membrane technology: A leapfrog approach to rural water treatment in developing countries?</title><summary>Lack of access to safe drinking water remains a present concern in many developing countries, particularly in rural locations. Membrane water treatment technologies have the potential to remove microbiological and chemical contaminants reliably and simultaneously from a wide range of water sources. When powered by renewable energy, these systems are autonomous and have the ability to 'leapfrog' over installation of traditional infrastructure for electricity and water supply to reach remote communities. In this paper, current estimated costs for water, membrane plants and infrastructure are compared to indicate the window of opportunity for these exciting renewable energy powered membrane (RE-membrane) technologies. General estimated costs for decentralized membrane systems are within the range of some untreated water costs in developing countries. Specific system costs, however, are very process and location dependent. The appropriateness of a successful approach thus depends partially on careful examination of these parameters. problem: 为我调研AI算法能否提升现有电子学读出时幅修正方法

## 摘要

电子学时幅转换（TAC）通过将时间间隔线性映射为电压，是获取时间分辨信息的成熟手段，其核心电路原理清晰且已被广泛工程化，例如ORTEC时间-电压转换器的描述和TOF电子学原型设计均验证了该路径的可行性<cite id="7"></cite><cite id="27"></cite>。然而，传统TAC的线性积分架构对元件漂移、阈值不匹配和短脉冲幅度敏感等固有缺陷，会引入系统误差并限制动态范围，这在声发射、粒子TOF和超声检测等应用中已被实测观察到<cite id="43"></cite><cite id="23"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>。现代AI算法在时间-信号处理领域已展现出提升时间拉伸质量、校正非线性、增强鲁棒性的潜力，尤其在语音、地震和医学超声中已有数据驱动方法超越传统相位插值方案<cite id="14"></cite><cite id="15"></cite><cite id="13"></cite>。因此，AI算法有望通过后处理或嵌入式校正补偿TAC链路的非理想性，但需结合具体前端误差特性进行适配设计。

## 电子学时幅转换方法的原理与局限

TAC的基本思想是利用恒流积分将时间间隔转化为与t成正比的电压脉冲，其输出幅度V=It/C直接映射时间，这一原理在ORTEC文档中被清晰阐述，并通过ADC或多道分析器构建时间谱<cite id="7"></cite>。在TOF探测器中，前端读出电子学原型设计明确要求时间分辨率中仅允许FEE贡献小于25 ps，表明电子学路径的精度目标和工程实现的成熟度<cite id="27"></cite>。然而，实际系统中积分器的漂移、比较阈值偏移和输入电流等非理想因素会导致线性度下降，例如声发射仪的实测误差分析指出TAC存在非线性并提出修正方法<cite id="43"></cite>；高计数率MRPC时间测量的刻度分析也揭示了电子学噪声和非线性对TOF分辨率的显著影响<cite id="23"></cite>。此外，超声检测中的声时修正公式和测量误差分析进一步说明了传播介质和耦合条件对时间基准的扰动，以及校正的必要性<cite id="18"></cite>。

## AI算法在时间处理中的进展与适用性

AI驱动的时间拉伸和校正方法已在多个领域取得进展。基于深度神经网络的语音时间拉伸（如WaveNet和Tacotron）通过端到端建模实现了自然的变速而不破坏音质，这与传统基于相位插值的算法形成对比<cite id="14"></cite>。在地震勘探中，深度学习的时频域方法在速度/深度建模、反演和时间-幅度联合变换中均表现出超越传统物理建模的潜力，例如深度地震勘探的综述指出AI方法在速度建模和反演中的优势<cite id="15"></cite>。医学超声领域，卷积神经网络已被用于超声心动图的帧率提升，通过数据驱动的插值和补全策略改善时间分辨率<cite="16"></cite>。值得注意的是，针对传统时间编码器的非线性，已有研究提出自适应校正策略，例如基于神经网络的TDC非线性补偿方法，通过学习和校正时间残差提升测量精度<cite id="54"></cite>。

## AI算法能否提升现有电子学时幅修正方法

AI算法可作为后处理校正或嵌入式补偿模块，提升TAC链路的时间精度与鲁棒性。对于积分漂移和阈值偏移等系统误差，自适应校正网络（如基于LSTM或Transformer的误差建模）可在线估计并补偿偏移项，类似于电压-时间转换器中提出的周期性自动校正机制<cite id="42"></cite><cite id="43"></cite>。针对比较器阈值不匹配，神经网络可学习跨通道/时间的偏移分布并进行归一化校正，这与时间-数字转换器中非线性补偿的思路一致<cite id="54"></cite>。此外，短脉冲幅度不足导致积分不足的问题，可通过脉冲幅度估计与插值算法结合AI预测，补充积分量以提升动态范围，这与超声检测中脉冲幅度测量与时间修正的耦合需求相符<cite id="43"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>。在粒子TOF场景中，AI还可用于多通道时间对齐与抖动抑制，例如基于深度学习的时序对齐算法可提升时间分辨率，这与高能物理实验中MRPC刻度分析的挑战相关<cite id="23"></cite>。

## 实施路径与注意事项

- 嵌入式校正：将轻量级神经网络集成到读出链中，直接处理TAC积分器输出，补偿漂移和阈值偏移，例如基于残差网络的周期性校正模块<cite id="42"></cite><cite id="54"></cite>。
- 后处理校正：利用AI模型对TAC时间谱进行非线性校正，尤其适用于多通道系统的时间对齐与抖动抑制<cite id="54"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>。
- 动态范围增强：结合脉冲幅度估计与AI插值算法，补偿短脉冲积分不足，提升动态范围，需注意幅度与时间测量的耦合特性<cite id="43"></cite><cite id="18"></cite>。
- 数据驱动适配：需基于具体电子学链路的实测误差特性训练模型，而非依赖通用语音/地震数据，以确保泛化性与鲁棒性<cite id="14"></cite><cite id="15"></cite>。

## 结论

现有电子学时幅转换方法在原理和工程实现上是可靠的，但受限于积分漂移、阈值偏移和短脉冲幅度等非理想因素，其精度和动态范围存在提升空间。AI算法在时间拉伸、非线性校正和抖动抑制方面已展现出显著优势，通过后处理或嵌入式校正模块可有效补偿TAC链路的系统误差，从而提升时幅修正效果。然而，成功实施需结合具体应用的电子学特性进行数据驱动适配，以确保模型的泛化性与测量精度<cite id="43"></cite><cite id="23"></cite><cite id="18"></cite><cite id="54"></cite><cite id="14"></cite><cite id="15"></cite>。

# Executive Summary

Quantum internet research is accelerating across academia and industry, with large-scale national testbeds, quantum repeater prototypes, and international standardization efforts converging toward a practical network stack. Europe’s Quantum Internet Alliance (QIA) has established a blueprint for interoperability and aims to demonstrate a 5-node experimental network by 2025, while China’s Micius satellite and quantum backbone, the U.S. Department of Energy’s nationwide prototype target by 2030, and Europe’s EAGLE-1 QKD satellite mission mark the leading national trajectories<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="8"></cite>. This report evaluates ten research groups and consortia most likely to lead the next phase of quantum networking, ranking them by combination of testbed scale, quantum repeater progress, stack/operating system leadership, satellite QKD capability, and public funding/standardization influence<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="20"></cite><cite id="24"></cite>.

# Methodology

We selected ten groups based on recent milestones and strategic positioning: QIA (Europe-wide coordination and QNodeOS), QuTech/TNO/TU Delft (stack and testbed leadership), University of Science and Technology of China (USTC/CAS) (satellite QKD and backbone), National Institute of Informatics (NII)/Kyoto University (quantum repeater and network stack), University of Tokyo (national backbone), University of Bristol/Cambridge (multi-technology fiber network), University of Stuttgart (quantum repeater prototype), IonQ (networking infrastructure and acquisitions), Deutsche Telekom Innovation Laboratories + Qunnect (high-fidelity entanglement over deployed fiber), and the European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI) (pan‑Europe network and satellite roadmap)<cite id="19"></cite><cite id="23"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="17"></cite><cite id="30"></cite><cite id="47"></cite><cite id="40"></cite><cite id="13"></cite><cite id="11"></cite>. Where possible, we assessed publication venues, leadership backgrounds, funding sources, and project scope; where evidence was limited, we note uncertainties<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="20"></cite><cite id="24"></cite>.

# Ten Most Promising Quantum Networking Groups and Consortia

## 1. Quantum Internet Alliance (QIA) – Europe
- Scope and impact: Europe’s largest coordinated effort, with 42 partners and a 25M€ budget; launched a blueprint for interoperable quantum stacks and aims to demonstrate a 5-node experimental network by 2025<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>.
- Publications and standards: Helped draft the IRTF application scenarios RFC 9583 and leads standardization via QuINSA; QNodeOS was highlighted in Nature<cite id="3"></cite><cite id="24"></cite><cite id="37"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: Founded by the Paris Centre for Quantum Computing, ICFO, and University of Innsbruck, and is part of the EU Quantum Technologies Flagship<cite id="19"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: 25M€ consortium with national and industrial members; active in testbeds and stack development<cite id="17"></cite>.
- Assessment: Strongest position to deliver an interoperable stack and multi-node testbed; likely to shape global standards<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="24"></cite>.

## 2. QuTech (TNO/TU Delft) – Netherlands
- Scope and impact: Coordinated the Dutch quantum internet testbed and contributed to the QIA stack; active in quantum memories and network protocols<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: TNO and TU Delft have long-standing leadership in quantum technologies and network integration<cite id="17"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: Part of the QIA consortium and national testbeds; integrated with quantum computing and memory research<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>.
- Assessment: Strong technical depth in network protocols and memories; central to European integration<cite id="23"></cite>.

## 3. University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)/Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) – China
- Scope and impact: Launched Micius, demonstrated satellite‑to‑ground entanglement distribution, and expanded a national quantum backbone; highlighted in Nature<cite id="28"></cite><cite id="11"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: Pioneers in satellite QKD and quantum communications; world-class teams in theory and experiment<cite id="28"></cite><cite id="11"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: National flagship programs and backbone deployments; extensive satellite missions<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Assessment: Unmatched satellite QKD capability; likely to lead space‑ground integration<cite id="28"></cite><cite id="11"></cite>.

## 4. National Institute of Informatics (NII)/Kyoto University – Japan
- Scope and impact: Built Japan’s quantum backbone and is developing a quantum internet stack; reported progress on quantum repeaters<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: NII has been a central Japanese player in quantum communications and networking<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: National backbone and stack development; quantum repeater research<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>.
- Assessment: Strong national backbone and stack work; advancing repeater technology<cite id="23"></cite>.

## 5. University of Tokyo – Japan
- Scope and impact: Operates Japan’s quantum backbone and collaborates on national quantum internet testbeds<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: Leading Japanese university in quantum communications and infrastructure<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: Backbone operations and national testbed integration<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Assessment: Central to Japan’s terrestrial backbone; integration with national testbeds<cite id="11"></cite>.

## 6. University of Bristol and University of Cambridge – United Kingdom
- Scope and impact: Demonstrated the UK’s first long‑distance, multi‑technology quantum network using standard fiber and multiple quantum‑secure techniques<cite id="30"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: Renowned groups in quantum communications and networking<cite id="30"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: OFC 2025 demonstration; part of broader UK quantum research ecosystem<cite id="30"></cite>.
- Assessment: Strong experimental networking capability; multi‑technology integration<cite id="30"></cite>.

## 7. University of Stuttgart – Germany
- Scope and impact: Made a milestone on quantum repeaters, a key bottleneck for long‑distance quantum networks<cite id="26"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: IHFG group with semiconductor optics expertise<cite id="26"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: Part of the German quantum repeater.Net consortium; national funding for quantum repeaters<cite id="10"></cite>.
- Assessment: Leading repeater research; critical for overcoming distance limits<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="10"></cite>.

## 8. IonQ – United States
- Scope and impact: Aggressively assembling networking infrastructure via acquisitions (Entangled Networks, Qubitekk, ID Quantique, Lightsynq, Capella); Lightsynq brings repeater and memory tech; Capella strengthens space‑based QKD ambitions<cite id="43"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: Formerly a pure quantum computing company, pivoting to networking with strategic acquisitions<cite id="43"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: Private capital and acquisitions; targeting end‑to‑end communication components<cite id="43"></cite>.
- Assessment: Fastest‑moving private player assembling repeaters, memories, and satellites; potential to scale quickly<cite id="43"></cite>.

## 9. Deutsche Telekom Innovation Laboratories (T‑Lab) + Qunnect – Germany/USA/Netherlands
- Scope and impact: Demonstrated sustained, high‑fidelity entangled‑photon transmission across 30 km of commercially deployed fiber for 17 days<cite id="13"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: T‑Lab’s telecom engineering combined with Qunnect’s quantum networking expertise<cite id="13"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: T‑Lab’s fiber test track; integration with commercial fiber infrastructure<cite id="13"></cite>.
- Assessment: Strong operational telecom integration; robust entanglement over deployed fiber<cite id="13"></cite>.

## 10. European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI)
- Scope and impact: Building a secure, pan‑Europe quantum network with fiber and satellite (EAGLE‑1); second after China’s satellite QKD<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Leadership and background: European Commission coordination with national labs and operators<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Funding and projects: EU‑funded infrastructure and satellite mission<cite id="11"></cite>.
- Assessment: Strong political and funding backing; likely to be the first continent‑wide quantum network<cite id="11"></cite>.

# Comparative Analysis by Dimension

- Interoperable stack and operating system: QIA’s QNodeOS and RFC 9583 application scenarios position Europe to lead standardization and stack interoperability<cite id="24"></cite><cite id="3"></cite>.
- Multi‑node testbeds: QIA aims for a 5‑node experimental network by 2025; the UK demonstrated a long‑distance multi‑technology network<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="30"></cite>.
- Quantum repeaters: Stuttgart and Germany’s QR.N consortium are at the forefront; NII/Kyoto and QIA are integrating repeater research into national stacks<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="10"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>.
- Satellite QKD: USTC/CAS (Micius) and EuroQCI (EAGLE‑1) are the leading space‑based programs; IonQ’s acquisition of Capella adds satellite ambitions<cite id="28"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="43"></cite>.
- Funding and national programs: The EU’s QIA and EuroQCI have large consortia; the U.S. DOE targets a nationwide prototype by 2030; Japan’s NII and University of Tokyo operate backbones and stacks<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="8"></cite>.

# Leading Candidates to Shape the Future

- Most likely to deliver an interoperable stack and multi‑node testbed: QIA (Europe)<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="24"></cite>.
- Strongest repeater progress: Stuttgart and Germany’s QR.N consortium<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="10"></cite>.
- Strongest satellite QKD capability: USTC/CAS (China) and EuroQCI (Europe)<cite id="28"></cite><cite id="11"></cite>.
- Fastest‑moving private networking infrastructure: IonQ (U.S.)<cite id="43"></cite>.
- Strongest telecom integration and operational testbeds: Deutsche Telekom Innovation Laboratories + Qunnect<cite id="13"></cite>.
- Strongest national backbone and stack integration: NII/Kyoto and University of Tokyo (Japan); QuTech and University of Bristol/Cambridge (Europe)<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="23"></cite><cite id="30"></cite>.

# Uncertainties and Outlook

Despite strong progress, long‑distance repeater networks and space‑ground integration remain technically challenging; success will depend on sustained funding, standardization, and cross‑platform interoperability<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="23"></cite>. The U.S. DOE’s 2030 prototype target and EuroQCI’s satellite roadmap suggest near‑term national deployments, while QIA’s stack and QNodeOS may become the de facto reference<cite id="8"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="24"></cite>. IonQ’s rapid acquisition strategy could accelerate commercial components, but integration into end‑to‑end networks will require ecosystem cooperation<cite id="43"></cite>.

# Conclusion

The ten groups and consortia above span testbeds, repeaters, stacks, and satellites, and collectively represent the most viable path to a practical quantum internet. QIA is best positioned to deliver an interoperable stack and multi‑node network, while USTC/CAS and EuroQCI lead satellite QKD, Stuttgart and QR.N lead repeaters, and IonQ and T‑Lab+Qunnect offer strong private-sector integration and operational robustness<cite id="23"></cite><cite id="24"></cite><cite id="28"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="26"></cite><cite id="10"></cite><cite id="43"></cite><cite id="13"></cite>.

problem: 收集整理目前非接触式感知领域做的最好的算法策略，并为我评估他们的输入信号与准确率

## Executive summary

Non-contact sensing has matured into a multi-modal field with complementary strengths across radar, Wi‑Fi, acoustic, vision, inertial, thermal, and magnetic modalities. Radar (especially FMCW millimeter wave) is robust to lighting and privacy, Wi‑Fi CSI enables device-free sensing, acoustic systems (ultrasonic and audio echo) offer high-resolution micro-gesture recognition, vision remains strong for rich appearance and RGB‑D interactions, inertial sensors improve wearability, thermal imaging is privacy-friendly and low‑light, and magnetic sensing adds directional, touchless control. Each modality has distinct input requirements and accuracy profiles; the best reported accuracies are often in controlled settings, and robustness and generalization remain open challenges across populations and environments<cite id="87"></cite><cite id="17"></cite><cite id="11"></cite><cite id="47"></cite><cite id="92"></cite><cite id="76"></cite><cite id="97"></cite>.

## Best-performing algorithm strategies by modality

### Radar (FMCW millimeter wave)

Radar is a strong non-contact modality for gesture recognition and vital-sign monitoring due to its robustness to lighting and privacy concerns. Recent surveys summarize FMCW radar pipelines—data acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification—and report dynamic gesture recognition results; they also highlight challenges such as generalization and real-time performance in complex scenes<cite id="87"></cite>. Radar is also widely used for contactless vital-sign monitoring (respiration, heart rate), demonstrating its reliability in non-contact sensing applications<cite id="89"></cite>.

### Wi‑Fi CSI (device-free sensing)

Device-free gesture recognition using Wi‑Fi channel state information (CSI) has seen significant progress. A comprehensive survey classifies model-based and learning-based approaches, summarizes preprocessing, feature extraction, and environmental factors, and discusses recognition accuracy and challenges for CSI-based device-free sensing<cite id="17"></cite>. Early device-free systems demonstrated sensing through walls and tracking behind closed doors via MIMO interference nulling and RF beam tracking, establishing CSI as a powerful non-contact signal source<cite id="34"></cite>.

### Acoustic sensing (ultrasonic echo and audio Doppler)

Acoustic sensing leverages commodity speakers and microphones to sense echoes or Doppler shifts for micro-gesture recognition. AudioGest uses a single built-in audio pair to detect hand movements around devices with up to 96% accuracy by turning the device into an active sonar<cite id="11"></cite>. AudioTouch recognizes micro-gestures and touch-force levels with high accuracy using piezo elements on the back of the hand<cite id="12"></cite>. UltraGesture achieves an average accuracy greater than 99% for 12 gestures (including finger motions) by modeling channel impulse responses and using convolutional neural networks<cite id="35"></cite>. A survey of ubiquitous acoustic sensing on IoT devices provides a framework for signal generation and extraction across temporal, spatial, and spectral information, covering hardware and applications<cite id="47"></cite>.

### Vision and RGB‑D sensing

Vision-based hand gesture recognition has a long history and continues to be strong for rich appearance and RGB‑D interactions. A survey of hand gesture recognition in HCI organizes methods by 3D hand models versus image appearance models, noting computational hurdles for real-time 3D modeling and the effectiveness of appearance-based approaches under constraints<cite id="26"></cite>. RGB‑D systems can achieve real-time hand motion capture and gesture matching with contour models and reliable tracking under varying lighting conditions<cite id="27"></cite>. Reviews of RGB‑D gesture recognition highlight applications and challenges, including robustness and generalization across subjects<cite id="28"></cite>. Thermal imaging is a privacy-friendly alternative to RGB for gesture recognition, with low-resolution thermal cameras achieving up to 98.5% accuracy on embedded devices and enabling non-contact sign language recognition<cite id="76"></cite>.

### Inertial sensing (IMU)

Inertial measurement units (IMUs) are wearable, unobtrusive, and increasingly accurate for gesture recognition. A dual-channel ANN decision fusion framework combining IMU raw data and spectrogram images improves hand gesture intention recognition compared to traditional CNNs on IMU spectrograms<cite id="68"></cite>. Surface magnetomyography (sMMG) measures magnetic fields generated by muscle activity and enables generalizable gesture recognition with high robustness to subject differences, outperforming sEMG in cross-subject generalization and offering a wearable alternative<cite id="97"></cite>. Reviews emphasize fusion of kinematic and physiological signals (e.g., IMU + sEMG) to mitigate inter-subject variability and improve accuracy and generalization<cite id="69"></cite>.

### Thermal sensing

Thermal imaging is inherently privacy-preserving and operates in low-light or no-light conditions. A low-resolution 32×24 pixel thermal camera achieved 98.5% accuracy on an in-house dataset with 4,500 images and 59 ms inference per frame, demonstrating embedded feasibility for gesture recognition<cite id="76"></cite>. Thermal sensing has also been used for surface interaction and gesture recognition without cameras, enabling segmentation and detection above surfaces and touch discrimination<cite id="78"></cite>.

### Magnetic sensing

Magnetic sensing adds directional, touchless control via magnetosensitive e-skins and MMG. Reviews describe magnetosensitive e-skins that detect vector magnetic fields for motion and orientation tracking, complementing optical systems in challenging visibility conditions<cite id="60"></cite>. sMMG measures magnetic fields from motor units and enables generalizable gesture recognition with strong cross-subject performance, indicating a viable touchless modality for HCI<cite id="97"></cite>.

## Input signals and accuracy across modalities

- Radar (FMCW mmWave): Uses continuous-wave frequency-modulated radar signals; reports dynamic gesture recognition results and vital-sign monitoring, with challenges in generalization and real-time performance in complex scenes<cite id="87"></cite><cite id="89"></cite>.
- Wi‑Fi CSI: CSI from wireless transceivers; device-free gesture recognition with accuracy summaries and environmental sensitivity<cite id="17"></cite><cite id="34"></cite>.
- Acoustic (ultrasonic/audio): Commodity speakers and microphones emitting ultrasonic or audio signals and receiving echoes/Doppler; AudioGest (96% accuracy), AudioTouch, UltraGesture (>99% accuracy)<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="35"></cite><cite id="47"></cite>.
- Vision: RGB cameras; RGB‑D depth sensors; thermal cameras (privacy-friendly, low-light). Surveys and reviews cover accuracy and challenges<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite><cite id="28"></cite><cite id="76"></cite><cite id="78"></cite>.
- IMU: Wearable 3‑axis accelerometers and 3‑axis gyroscopes; dual-channel ANN fusion improves recognition; fusion with sEMG improves generalization<cite id="68"></cite><cite id="69"></cite>.
- sMMG: Wearable magnetic sensors measuring muscle-generated magnetic fields; generalizable gesture recognition with strong cross-subject performance<cite id="97"></cite>.

## Practical recommendations

- For robust, privacy-preserving gesture recognition in low-light or behind walls, radar and Wi‑Fi CSI are strong choices; radar excels for dynamic gestures and vital signs, while Wi‑Fi CSI enables device-free sensing with accuracy depending on environmental factors<cite id="87"></cite><cite id="89"></cite><cite id="17"></cite><cite id="34"></cite>.
- For micro-gesture and fine motor control, acoustic systems (ultrasonic echo and audio Doppler) deliver state-of-the-art accuracy (e.g., >99% for finger gestures) using commodity audio hardware<cite id="11"></cite><cite id="12"></cite><cite id="35"></cite>.
- For rich appearance and RGB‑D interactions, vision remains strong; thermal imaging is a privacy-friendly alternative with high accuracy on embedded devices<cite id="26"></cite><cite id="27"></cite><cite id="28"></cite><cite id="76"></cite>.
- For wearables and unobtrusive sensing, IMUs and sMMG offer high accuracy and generalization; IMU fusion with physiological signals improves robustness across users<cite id="68"></cite><cite id="69"></cite><cite id="97"></cite>.

## Open challenges and future directions

Across modalities, generalization across subjects and environments, real-time performance, and robustness to occlusions and varying conditions remain key challenges. Surveys emphasize the need for better generalization, feature fusion, and real-time capabilities in radar and non-contact sensing<cite id="87"></cite><cite id="104"></cite>. Vision reviews highlight gaps in continuous gesture recognition and the need for improved accuracy<cite id="92"></cite>. Acoustic sensing frameworks and device surveys outline hardware and algorithmic opportunities for IoT-based systems<cite id="47"></cite><cite id="104"></cite>. Magnetic sensing and sMMG show promise for touchless, generalizable control, but broader adoption requires wearable form factors and standardized datasets<cite id="60"></cite><cite id="97"></cite>.

## Supporting resources

- Open datasets for contactless sensing are curated to facilitate benchmarking across technologies, including collection scenarios, sample counts, and typical work baselines<cite id="104"></cite>.
- Reviews of non-contact sensing for structural monitoring and health provide broader context on principles and applications<cite id="105"></cite><cite id="107"></cite>.

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="camera-based device-free gesture recognition survey RGB-D depth CSI vision review" search_time="2026年5月16日11时40分星期六"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:26"><title>Visual Interpretation of Hand Gestures for Human-Computer Interaction: A Review</title><summary>The use of hand gestures provides an attractive alternative to cumbersome interface devices for human-computer interaction (HCI). In particular, visual interpretation of hand gestures can help in achieving the ease and naturalness desired for HCI. This has motivated a very active research area concerned with computer vision-based analysis and interpretation of hand gestures. This discussion is organized on the basis of the method used for modeling, analyzing, and recognizing gestures. Important differences in the gesture interpretation approaches arise depending on whether a 3D model of the human hand or an image appearance model of the human hand is used. 3D hand models offer a way of more elaborate modeling of hand gestures but lead to computational hurdles that have not been overcome given the real-time requirements of HCI. We also discuss implemented gestural systems as well as other potential applications of vision-based gesture recognition. Although the current progress is encouraging, further theoretical as well as computational advances are needed before gestures can be widely used for HCI.
